new_statements.quote: Kodia has a quinary, vigesimal system similar to that of other Kru languages. More completed data for numbers from 20 onwards needed. Tone marks used above areː v²=high; v⁴³=tone is low-mid on first syllable, and slightly higher that mid on second; first syllable seems 1, 1/2 times longer than second. Kodia or Kwadia is spoken by approximately 800 speakers in Bas-Sassandra district, Côte d'Ivoire.

Useful negative evidence: lists the 19 Kru languages for which Marchese's 1984 Atlas linguistique kru gives consonant systems (Aizi, Bassa, Bete, Cedepo, Dewoin, Dida de Lozoua, Dida F, Godie, Grebo, Guere, Klao, Koyo, Krahn, Kuwaa, Neyo, Niaboua, Seme, Tepo, Wobe) -- Kodia/Kwadia is not among them, so even the Atlas apparently has no phonological sketch of Kodia.

sources.citation: Hombert, Jean-Marie. 1984. Les systemes tonals des langues africaines: typologie et diachronie. Pholia 1: 113-164. Lyon: Centre de Recherches Linguistiques et Semiologiques, Universite Lumiere Lyon 2. (52-page offprint PDF with scanned text on the DDL Lyon server.)
sources.note: Family-level only: Kru languages have three or four level tones (after Marchese 1979), most also have contour tones (complementary in Kuwaa and Wobe, contrastive in Bassa), Wobe has the most complex system (14 tonal oppositions on monosyllables), consonant-tone interaction in Godie, Dewoin, Bassa, Kuwaa, and grammatical tone (aspect, pronouns, number) illustrated from Godie; the diachronic part reconstructs the register split. Kwadia appears solely in the list of eastern Kru languages; no tone count, no data and no stress/accent remark is given for it. Not a statement about this languoid; rec…
